name: FLOOD TILES
description: One of the oldest continuously played games in Meridian 88's recorded entertainment catalog, Flood Tiles is a 2��4 player abstract tile-laying game using 72 hexagonal ceramic tiles depicting rising water, infrastructure, and refuge points — a clear metaphor for the Great Lakes flooding events of the 2160s that shaped M88's geography. Players race to build viable refuge networks while flooding the other players' districts; the tiles are ceramic, weighty, and designed to last generations.
story_hooks: A Shelf community discovers that the original Flood Tiles rulebook, when decoded, contains a map of pre-flood infrastructure tunnels still accessible beneath M88.
A new tile variant appears on the market depicting current district borders — borders that haven't been publicly announced yet.
A Tier 5 collector hoards every original 2183 ceramic set, and someone on the Shelf wants to know exactly why.
